summary.text: 时 means “time” and is the standardized simplified form of 時. In 時, 日 marks the day/time category and 寺 is identified as a sound element; the available sound evidence is compatible with that analysis but does not prove its history.

formation.text: Traditional 時 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 日 contributes the day/time category, while 寺 supplies a sound cue. An earlier graph, 旹, places 之 above 日 and is also described as phonosemantic, with 之 supplying sound. In 时, 寺 was abbreviated to 寸; this graphic abbreviation does not establish 寸 as an independent meaning element.

components.text: In 時, 日 contributes the day/time category. It also appears below 之 in 旹; this analysis does not establish that the graph depicts the sun moving.
寺 is identified as the sound element in 時. Baxter–Sagart reconstructions are compatible with this role, though they do not prove its history. In 时, 寺 was abbreviated to 寸.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructed comparison is compatible with a sound cue but does not independently prove the phonetic history.

sound.text: In Old Chinese, both reconstructions contain *[d]ə, but 寺 has additional initial *s- and final *-ʔ-s material absent from 時.
Modern Mandarin 寺 sì and 時 shí differ; this current pair alone does not establish their ancient sound relationship.

components.text: In 旹, 之 is above 日 and is described as the sound element. This component belongs to 旹, not to 時 or current 时.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin pair zhī–shí does not establish the proposed ancient sound relation between 之 and 旹; the cited readings are local current-reading data.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings can be compared, but they do not establish the historical sound correspondence or which lexical use of 之 supplied the proposed sound.

history.text: The earliest secure graph described is Eastern Zhou 旹, with 之 above 日. Later forms often add 寺 as a sound element, producing 時. A Warring States inscription uses 旹 in a sense glossed “regularly.” Alleged oracle-bone examples remain disputed and have also been read as 之日, “this day.” The spoken word may be older than the surviving secure graph evidence.

In traditional 時, some manuscript forms write the lower part of 寺 as 寸. The standardized simplified form 时 continues a premodern abbreviation of 寺 to 寸; these graphic changes do not in themselves show a change in meaning.

uncertainties.text: Historical accounts identify 之 in 旹 and 寺 in 時 as sound elements, but the available comparisons do not fully demonstrate their historical sound relations. Proposed lexical explanations involving solar motion do not show that the graph depicts the sun moving.
The precise earliest lexical example remains unresolved. Early transmitted texts contain the time word, but their dating is separate from the secure dating of the graph.

senses.text: Abstract time is treated as the lexical core. Early transmitted texts use the word, though the precise date of the earliest lexical example is unresolved.
A Warring States inscription uses 旹 in a sense glossed “regularly.”
The character is used for a season or quarter, but the development and chronology of this sense are unresolved.
The character also means an era, age, or period; the development of these senses is not dated here.
A demonstrative use is reported, but its relationship to the time noun remains complex.

developments.text: Season or quarter is a recorded time-related sense, but no specific semantic path or chronology is established.

limitations.text: The “four seasons” gloss does not show that seasons were the original meaning or date the development of this sense.

takeaway.text: The 寸 in 时 results from abbreviating 寺; it is not independently established as a meaning element.

relationships.text: 日 contributes the day/time category in traditional 時.
寺 is identified as a sound element in 時; the available comparisons do not fully demonstrate the historical relation.

In 旹, 之 is above 日 and described as the sound element. Current Mandarin readings are available for comparison, but no corresponding historical reading for 旹 is supplied, so the ancient correspondence is not established by that pair.
旹 is described as an earlier graph that later forms often elaborated with 寺 as a sound element to make 時.
时 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 時 and continues a premodern abbreviated form in which 寺 was reduced to 寸.
